Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 61, verses 1–3:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies Allah, and He is the Mighty, the Wise (1). O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do? (2) It is greatly hateful to Allah that you say what you do not do (3).﴾

His saying, may His praise be exalted: ﴿Whatever is in the heavens﴾ of the seven [heavens] ﴿and whatever is on the earth﴾ of creation, submitting to Him in divinity and lordship, ﴿and He is the Mighty﴾ in His retribution against those among them who disobey Him and disbelieve in Him and oppose His command, ﴿the Wise﴾ in His management of them.

* *

And His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do?﴾

The Exalted says: O you who have believed, affirm Allah and His Messenger. Why do you say words that you do not confirm by action, your deeds contradicting your words? ﴿It is greatly hateful to Allah that you say what you do not do﴾. He says: Your saying what you do not do is greatly hateful in the sight of your Lord.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning the occasion on account of which this verse was revealed. Some of them said: It was revealed as a rebuke from Allah to a people among the believers who wished to know the best of deeds, so Allah informed them of it; then when they knew it, they fell short, so they were reproached with this verse.

Mention of those who said that:

Ali related to me, he said: Abu Salih related to us, he said: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do?﴾ He said: Some people among the believers, before jihad was enjoined, were saying: "We wish that Allah would guide us to the deeds most beloved to Him, so that we might act upon them." So Allah informed His Prophet that the deed most beloved to Him is faith in Allah without doubt, and striving against the people of disobedience who opposed faith and did not acknowledge it. Then when jihad was revealed, some of the believers disliked it and found its command burdensome, so Allah said: ﴿O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do?﴾

Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: My father related to me, he said: My paternal uncle related to me, he said: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do? It is greatly hateful to Allah that you say what you do not do﴾. He said: There were people who were saying: "By Allah, if only we knew what deeds are most beloved to Allah, we would do them." So Allah revealed to His Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do? It is greatly hateful...﴾ up to His words: ﴿as if they were a solid structure﴾, and He guided them to the deeds most beloved to Him.

Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Muhammad ibn Juhada, from Abu Salih, he said: They said: "If only we knew which deeds are most beloved and best to Allah." Then it was revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, shall I direct you to a transaction that will save you from a painful punishment?﴾ and they disliked it, so ﴿O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do?﴾ was revealed.

Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, he said: Abu Asim related to us, he said: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of Allah ﴿Why do you say what you do not do?﴾ ... up to His words ﴿solid structure﴾: among that, concerning a group of the Ansar, among whom was Abdullah ibn Rawaha, who said in a gathering: "If we knew which deeds are most beloved to Allah, we would act upon them until we die." So Allah revealed this concerning them. Then Abdullah ibn Rawaha said: "I will not cease to be a stationed fighter in the way of Allah until I die," and he was killed as a martyr.

Others said: Rather, this verse was revealed as a rebuke of a people among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), one of whom would boast of an act of good that he had not done, saying: "I did such and such," so Allah reproved them for boasting of what they had not done, as a falsehood.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding His words: ﴿Why do you say what you do not do?﴾ He said: It has reached me that it was concerning jihad: a man would say, "I fought and did," when he had not done so, and Allah admonished them concerning that with the most severe admonition.

Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His words: ﴿O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do?﴾ He warns them and teaches them, as you hear: ﴿It is greatly hateful to Allah﴾. And there were men who reported in battle something they had not done and had not accomplished, so Allah admonished them in that with an eloquent admonition, saying: ﴿O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do?﴾ ... up to His words: ﴿as if they were a solid structure﴾.

It was related to me from al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd related to us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words: ﴿Why do you say what you do not do?﴾ Allah revealed this concerning the man who says in battle what he did not do of striking, thrusting and killing. Allah said: ﴿It is greatly hateful to Allah that you say what you do not do﴾.

Others said: Rather, this is a rebuke from Allah to a people among the hypocrites, who were promising the believers victory while they were liars.

Mention of those who said that:

Yunus related to us, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding Allah's words: ﴿It is greatly hateful to Allah that you say what you do not do﴾: They would say to the Prophet (ﷺ) and his Companions: "If you go out, we will go out with you, and we will be in your support, and such and such"; so He informed them that it is ﴿greatly hateful to Allah that you say what you do not do﴾.

The most correct of these interpretations of the verse, in my view, is the view of those who said: It refers to those who said, "If we knew the deeds most beloved to Allah, we would act upon them," and then fell short in acting upon them after they had come to know them.

The reason I say this view is more fitting for it is that Allah, may His praise be exalted, addressed the believers with it, saying: ﴿O you who have believed﴾. Had it been revealed concerning the hypocrites, they would not have been addressed by name nor described as believers. And if they had described themselves as doing what they had not done, they would have deliberately uttered a lie, and that was not the attribute of these people. Rather, in my view, by their saying "If we knew the deeds most beloved to Allah, we would act upon them," they were hoping that if they knew, they would act. Then when they knew, the strength of some of them weakened from undertaking what they had hoped to undertake before knowledge, while others grew strong and undertook it, and for them was the merit and honour.

The grammarians differed concerning the meaning of that and the grammatical case of His words ﴿greatly hateful﴾ (kabura maqtan). Some of the grammarians of Basra said: His words ﴿It is greatly hateful to Allah﴾ mean: "Your hatred has become greatly hateful" (kabura maqtakum maqtan), then He said ﴿that you say what you do not do﴾ as the explanation of your saying. Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: His words ﴿O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do?﴾ — the Muslims were saying: "If we knew which deeds are most beloved to Allah, we would come to it, even if our lives and wealth were lost in it." Then when the day of Uhud came, they withdrew from the Prophet (ﷺ) until he was wounded on the head and his front tooth was broken, so He said ﴿Why do you say what you do not do?﴾, then He said ﴿It is greatly hateful to Allah﴾: that became greatly hateful, meaning "that" (an) is in the place of nominative, because "kabura" is like His saying: "Evil is a man, your brother" (bi'sa rajulan akhuka).

* *

And His saying: ﴿It is greatly hateful to Allah﴾

And in the sight of those who believe, there is a hidden subject in "kabura" that would be in the nominative case.

The correct view on this matter, in my opinion, is that His words ﴿maqtan﴾ are in the accusative as an explanation (tafsir), like the speaker's saying: "It became great as a saying, this saying."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 61, verse 4:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who fight in His cause in a row, as if they were a wall, joined firmly together (4)﴾

He, may He be exalted, says to those who said: "If we knew which deeds are most beloved to Allah, we would do them until we die": ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾ O people ﴿loves those who fight in His cause﴾ as if they were, meaning on His path and His religion to which He calls ﴿in a row﴾. He means by this that they fight the enemies of Allah lined up in ranks.

* *

And His saying: ﴿as if they were a wall, joined firmly together﴾

He says: they fight in the cause of Allah in a well-ordered row, as if in their standing there they were built walls that have been fitted together (ruṣṣa), meaning made firm and perfected, so that nothing gaps in them. Some of them used to say: it was built with lead (al-raṣāṣ).

Ahl al-ta'wil (the scholars of interpretation) said things similar to what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who fight in His cause in a row, as if they were a wall, joined firmly together﴾: Do you not see the owner of a building, how he does not like his building to be uneven? Likewise, Blessed and Exalted is He, His command is not uneven. Indeed Allah described the believers in their fighting as He described them in their prayer. So hold to the command of Allah, for it is a safeguard for whoever grasps it.

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who fight in His cause in a row, as if they were a wall, joined firmly together﴾. He said: "Those who confirmed their words with their deeds are these." He said: "And these did not confirm their words with deeds; when the Prophet ﷺ set out, they turned back from him and stayed behind."

Some scholars of knowledge used to say: Allah only said ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who fight in His cause in a row﴾ to indicate that fighting on foot is more beloved to Him than fighting on horseback, because horsemen do not line up in rows, whereas infantry do.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Sa'id ibn Amr al-Sakuni narrated to me, saying: Baqiyya ibn al-Walid narrated to us, from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Maryam, from Yahya ibn Jabir al-Ta'i, from Abu Bahriyya, who said: They used to dislike fighting on horseback and preferred fighting on the ground, based on the saying of Allah: ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who fight in His cause in a row, as if they were a wall, joined firmly together﴾. He said: Abu Bahriyya used to say: "If you see me turn around in the row, then strike me on my beard."

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 61, verse 5:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And [mention] when Moses said to his people, "O my people, why do you harm me while you know that I am the messenger of Allah to you?" So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate. And Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people.﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): And mention, O Muhammad, ﴿when Moses﴾ son of Imran ﴿said to his people, "O my people, why do you harm me while you know﴾ truly ﴿that I am the messenger of Allah to you"﴾.

* *

As for His words: ﴿So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate﴾

He means: when they turned away and transgressed from the straight path, Allah caused their hearts to deviate, meaning: Allah inclined their hearts away from it.

⁕ Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, he said: Hushaym related to us, he said: al-Awwam informed us, he said: Abu Ghalib related to us, from Abu Umamah, regarding His words: ﴿So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate﴾, he said: They are the Kharijites. ﴿And Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people﴾ means: And Allah does not grant success in reaching the truth to the people who chose disbelief over faith.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 61, verse 6:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And when Jesus, the son of Mary, said: O Children of Israel, indeed I am the messenger of Allah to you, confirming what came before me of the Torah, and giving glad tidings of a messenger who will come after me, whose name is Ahmad. But when he came to them with clear proofs, they said, "This is manifest magic."﴾ (61:6)

His, the Exalted's, saying: Mention also, O Muhammad, ﴿when Jesus, the son of Mary, said﴾ to his people from the Children of Israel: ﴿O Children of Israel, indeed I am the messenger of Allah to you, confirming what came before me of the Torah﴾ which was revealed to Moses ﴿and giving glad tidings﴾ I give you good news ﴿of a messenger who will come after me, whose name is Ahmad﴾.

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Mu'awiya ibn Salih informed me, from Sa'id ibn Suwayd, from Abd al-A'la ibn Hilal al-Sulami, from Irbad ibn Sariya, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Indeed I am written with Allah as the Seal of the Prophets, while Adam was still lying in his clay. I will inform you of the first of that: it is the supplication of my father Abraham, the glad tidings of Jesus concerning me, and the vision my mother saw; and likewise the mothers of the prophets see such visions. They saw that when they gave birth to me, a light came forth from them by which the palaces of Syria were illuminated."

﴿But when he came to them with clear proofs﴾: he says, when Ahmad came to them with the clear proofs, meaning the evidences which Allah gave him as proofs of his prophethood, ﴿they said, "This is manifest magic"﴾: he says, what he brought is nothing but that I am a magician.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 61, verse 7:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah while he is being invited to Islam? And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Who is greater in injustice and transgression than one who invents a lie against Allah, and that is the saying of their speaker to the Prophet (ﷺ): "He is a sorcerer," and "what he brought is sorcery." So likewise is his fabrication of a lie against Allah, while he is being invited to Islam, meaning: when he is called to enter Islam, he says about Allah what is false and fabricates against Him falsehood. ﴿And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾ means: Allah does not grant success to the people who have wronged themselves by their disbelief in Him, so as to reach the truth.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 61, verse 8–9:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿They want to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths, but Allah will perfect His light, though the disbelievers dislike it﴾ (8).

Allah, exalted is His remembrance, says: These who say to Muhammad ﷺ, "This is clear sorcery," want ﴿to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths﴾, meaning they want to nullify the truth with which Allah sent Muhammad ﷺ, with their mouths, that is, with their saying that he is a sorcerer and that what he brought is sorcery. ﴿But Allah will perfect His light﴾, meaning: Allah makes the truth manifest, displays His religion, and gives victory to Muhammad ﷺ, peace be upon him, over those who oppose him; that is the perfecting of His light. By "light" in this place is meant Islam.

Ibn Zayd used to say: by it is meant the Qur'an.

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths﴾: "the light of the Qur'an."

The reciters differed regarding the recitation of His words ﴿and Allah will perfect His light﴾. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra, and some of the Kufans, recited ﴿mutimmun nūrihi﴾ with nasb (fatha on the final letter of mutimm, the nunation). Some reciters of Mecca and the majority of the reciters of Kufa recited ﴿mutimmu﴾ without tanwin, nūrihi with khafd (kasra, as a genitive construction). These are two well-known readings, close in meaning, and whichever of them the reciter reads is correct in our view.

* *

And His words: ﴿though the disbelievers dislike it﴾.

He says: Allah is the one who makes His religion manifest and gives victory to His Messenger, even if the disbelievers in Allah dislike it.

* *

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, that He may make it prevail over all religion, though the polytheists dislike it﴾ (9).

Allah, exalted is His remembrance, says: Allah is the One who sent His Messenger Muhammad with guidance and the religion of truth, meaning with the clarification of the truth, and the religion of truth, meaning: and with the religion of Allah, which is Islam.

* *

And His words: ﴿that He may make it prevail over all religion﴾.

He says: that He may make His true religion, with which He sent His Messenger, prevail over every religion other than it. That will be at the descent of Jesus son of Mary, when the community becomes one, and there will be no religion other than Islam.

As:

We have already mentioned the differences of those who differ regarding the meaning of His words ﴿that He may make it prevail over all religion﴾, and the correct view in our opinion on that matter, with its reasons, has been stated earlier, in a way that makes repeating it in this place unnecessary.

* And 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja'far narrated to me, saying: al-Aswad ibn al-'Ala' narrated to us, from Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from 'Aisha, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say: "Night and day will not pass until al-Lat and al-'Uzza are worshipped." He said: "There will be what Allah wills of that. Then Allah will send a pleasant wind, and it will take the soul of everyone who has in his heart the weight of a mustard seed of good, so there will remain only those who have no good in them, and they will return to the religion of their fathers."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 61, verses 10–11:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, shall I guide you to a transaction that will save you from a painful punishment?﴾ [10] ﴿You believe in Allah and His Messenger, and strive in the way of Allah with your wealth and your lives. That is best for you, if you only knew.﴾ [11]

He, may His mention be exalted, says: "O you who have believed, shall I guide you to a transaction that will save you from a painful punishment" – painful, meaning distressing, which is the punishment of Hell. Then He, may His majesty be exalted, explained to us what that transaction is that saves us from the painful punishment, saying: ﴿You believe in Allah and His Messenger﴾, Muhammad (ﷺ).

If someone says: How is it said, ﴿You believe in Allah and His Messenger﴾, when they have already been addressed as ﴿O you who have believed﴾, describing them as believers? The answer to that is similar to our answer regarding His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, believe in Allah﴾, and the explanation of that has already been given in its place, sufficiently so that it need not be repeated.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and strive in the way of Allah with your wealth and your lives﴾

He, may His mention be exalted, says: and strive in the religion of Allah and His path which He has legislated for you, with your wealth and your lives. ﴿That is best for you﴾, meaning: your belief in Allah and His Messenger, and your striving in the way of Allah with your wealth and your lives, ﴿is best for you﴾ over neglecting that and being remiss. ﴿If you only knew﴾ the harms and benefits of things.

It is reported that in the reading of Abdullah (Ibn Mas'ud) it is ﴿Believe in Allah﴾ in the imperative form. The transaction was clarified by His saying: ﴿shall I guide you to a transaction that will save you﴾, and it was explained by His saying: ﴿You believe in Allah﴾, and He did not say "that you believe" (an tu'minu), because the Arabs, when they explain a noun by a verb, sometimes keep "an" in that explanation and sometimes drop it. They say to a man: "Would you like some good, that we get up and visit so-and-so?" and "Would you like some good that you get up and visit so-and-so?" – with "an" and without it. Among what has come in both forms is His saying: ﴿So let man look at his food, that We (anna) ...﴾ with the opening "an" (anna) and with "inna" (the kasra). The fath in "an" is the dialect of those who insert "an" after "yaqum" (as in "hal laka fi khayrin an taqum"), and the kasra is the dialect of those who omit "an" after "taqum" ; and from it is His saying: ﴿So look how was the end of their plotting, that We (anna) destroyed them﴾, with "anna" and "inna dammarnahum", as we have explained.

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, shall I guide you to a transaction that will save you﴾ ... the verse. Had Allah not clarified it and pointed the believers to it, men would have been anxious to know it, so that they would be eager to seek it. But Allah has guided you to it and informed you of it, saying: ﴿You believe in Allah and His Messenger, and strive in the way of Allah with your wealth and your lives. That is best for you, if you only knew.﴾

⁕ Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, he said: Qatadah recited: ﴿shall I guide you to a transaction that will save you from a painful punishment. You believe in Allah and His Messenger, and strive in the way of Allah﴾, and said: "Praise be to Allah who has clarified it."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 61, verse 12–13:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿He will forgive you your sins and admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow, and pleasant dwellings in gardens of perpetual residence. That is the great triumph﴾

His, may He be exalted and remembered, says: Your Lord will cover over your sins for you if you do that, so He will pardon you and forgive you. ﴿And admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾ means: and He will admit you into orchards beneath whose trees rivers flow. ﴿And pleasant dwellings﴾ means: and He will also admit you to pleasant dwellings. ﴿In gardens of perpetual residence﴾ means: in orchards of lasting abode, from which there is no departure.

* *

And His saying: ﴿That is the great triumph﴾

means: that is the great deliverance from the torment of the Hereafter and its terrors.

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 61, verse 14:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And another [favour] you love: victory from Allah and an imminent conquest. So give good tidings to the believers (13). O you who have believed, be helpers of Allah, as Jesus, the son of Mary, said to the disciples, "Who are my helpers for Allah?" The disciples said, "We are the helpers of Allah." And a faction of the Children of Israel believed, and a faction disbelieved. So We supported those who believed against their enemy, and they became dominant (14).﴾

The scholars of Arabic grammar differed regarding how to parse His words, "And another [favour]" (wa-ukhrā). Some of the grammarians of Basra said: its meaning is "and another commerce" (wa-tijāratun ukhrā). According to this view, ukhrā must be in the genitive position (khafḍ), being coordinated (ʿaṭf) with His words, "Shall I direct you to a commerce that will save you from a painful punishment?" It may also possibly be in the nominative position as an inceptive (ibtidāʾ). Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: it is in the nominative position, meaning: "and for you there is another [favour] in this world, along with the reward of the Hereafter." Then He said, "victory from Allah" (naṣrun min Allāh), explaining the "another" (al-ukhrā).

The correct view in this matter, in my opinion, is the second view, namely that it means: "and for you there is another [favour] that you love," because His words, "victory from Allah and an imminent conquest," clarify that His words, "and another," are in the nominative position. Had it come in the genitive, it would have been fine to make His words, "and another," a coordination with His words, "commerce," so the meaning of the sentence would then be, if it were read in the genitive: "and [for] another gift that you love." The meaning of the sentence, when the matter is as you have described, is: "Shall I direct you to a commerce that will save you from a painful punishment? You believe in Allah and His Messenger, He will forgive you your sins and admit you into gardens beneath which rivers flow, and for you there is another gift besides that in this world that you love: victory from Allah over your enemies, and an imminent conquest that He will hasten for you."

﴿And give good tidings to the believers﴾: The Exalted says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: "And give good tidings, O Muhammad, to the believers of Allah's support for them over their enemy, and a swift conquest for them."

* *

And His words: ﴿O you who have believed, be helpers of Allah﴾

The readers differed concerning the recitation of this. The majority of the readers of Medina and Basra recited it as ﴿kūnū anṣāra Allāh﴾ with tanwin on "anṣār." The majority of the readers of Kufa recited it with "anṣār" annexed to Allah (idafa).

The correct view in this matter, in my opinion, is that both are well-known recitations, sound in meaning, so whichever of them the reader recites is correct. The meaning of the sentence is: "O you who have affirmed Allah and His Messenger, be helpers of Allah, as Jesus, the son of Mary, said to the disciples, 'Who are my helpers in the cause of Allah?'" meaning: "Who among you are my helpers toward the support of Allah for me?"

Qatadah used to say concerning this:

⁕ Bishr narrated to me, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿O you who have believed, be helpers of Allah, as Jesus, the son of Mary, said to the disciples, "Who are my helpers for Allah?" The disciples said, "We are the helpers of Allah"﴾, he said: "Allah has had helpers from this community who strive for His Book and His right." It was mentioned to us that seventy-two men of the Helpers pledged allegiance to him on the night of al-'Aqabah. It was mentioned to us that some of them said: "Do you know on what you are pledging allegiance to this man? You are pledging to fight all the Arabs, or that they submit." It was mentioned to us that a man said: "O Prophet of Allah, stipulate for your Lord and for yourself whatever you wish." He said: "I stipulate for my Lord that you worship Him and do not associate anything with Him, and I stipulate for myself that you protect me from what you protect yourselves and your sons from." They said: "If we do that, what will we have, O Prophet of Allah?" He said: "For you is victory in this world, and Paradise in the Hereafter." They did so, and Allah fulfilled [His promise]."

⁕ Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, he said: Qatadah recited, ﴿Be helpers of Allah, as Jesus, the son of Mary, said to the disciples, "Who are my helpers for Allah?"﴾ and said: "That was so, by the praise of Allah. Seventy men came to him and pledged allegiance to him at al-'Aqabah, and they supported him and sheltered him until Allah made His religion manifest." They said: "No tribe of the heavens has been named with a name that was not theirs before that."

⁕ Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: "The disciples were all from Quraysh: Abu Bakr, 'Umar, 'Ali, Hamzah, Ja'far, Abu 'Ubaydah, 'Uthman ibn Maz'un, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, 'Uthman, Talhah ibn 'Ubayd Allah, and al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam."

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, he said: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the words of Allah, ﴿Who are my helpers for Allah?﴾ He said: "Who will follow me to Allah?"

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Maysarah, from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, he said: Ibn 'Abbas was asked about the disciples, and he said: "They were named for the whiteness of their garments; they were fishermen."

⁕ It was related to me from al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd narrated to us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His words, "the disciples": "They are launderers in the Nabataean language; a launderer is called hawwari." The explanation of the meaning of hawwari, with its evidences and the disagreements of those who differed about it, has already been given earlier, so it suffices without repeating it.

* *

And His words: ﴿The disciples said, "We are the helpers of Allah"﴾

He means: they said, "We are the helpers of Allah in what He sent His prophets with of truth."

* *

And His words: ﴿So a faction of the Children of Israel believed, and a faction disbelieved﴾

He, glorified is His praise, says: a faction of the Children of Israel believed in Jesus, and a faction of them disbelieved in him.

The scholars of interpretation said the same as what we have said about this.

Those who said so:

⁕ Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, he said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from al-Minhal, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, he said: "When Allah willed to raise Jesus to heaven, he went out to his companions while they were in a house, twelve men, from a spring in the house, and his head was dripping water. He said: 'Among you there will be one who will disbelieve in me twelve times after he has believed in me.' Then he said: 'Which of you will have my likeness cast upon him, and be killed in my place, and be with me in my rank?' A young man, the youngest of them, stood and said, 'I.' He said to him: 'Sit down.' Then he repeated it to them, and the young man stood and said, 'I.' He said: 'Yes, you are that one.' So the likeness of Jesus was cast upon him, and Jesus was raised from an opening in the house to heaven. The pursuers came from the Jews, and they took his likeness, and killed him and crucified him, and one of them disbelieved in him twelve times after he had believed in him. Then they split into three sects. One sect said: 'Allah was among us as long as He willed, then He ascended to heaven,' and these are the Jacobites. One sect said: 'The son of Allah was among us as long as Allah willed, then He raised him to Himself,' and these are the Nestorians. And one sect said: 'The servant of Allah and His Messenger was among us as long as Allah willed, then Allah raised him to Himself,' and these are the Muslims. Then the two disbelieving sects allied against the Muslim sect and killed it, and Islam remained obliterated until Allah sent Muhammad ﷺ. Then a faction of the Children of Israel believed, and a faction disbelieved, meaning the faction of the Children of Israel that disbelieved in the time of Jesus, and the faction that believed in the time of Jesus. So We supported those who believed against their enemy, meaning: in manifesting Muhammad ﷺ's religion, the religion of the disbelievers, so they became dominant." And His words, "So We supported those who believed against their enemy," mean: We strengthened those who believed from the two factions of the Children of Israel against their enemy, those among them who disbelieved in Muhammad ﷺ, by his confirming them that Jesus is the servant of Allah and His Messenger, and his denying the one who said he is God, and the one who said he is the son of Allah, exalted is He. So they became dominant, so the believing faction became dominant over their disbelieving enemy among them.

The scholars of interpretation said the same as what we have said about this.

Those who said so:

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Hilali narrated to me, he said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning ﴿So We supported those who believed against their enemy﴾: "We strengthened them."

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Simak, from Ibrahim, concerning ﴿So a faction of the Children of Israel believed, and a faction disbelieved﴾: "When Allah sent Muhammad, and the confirmation of those who believed in Jesus was revealed, the proof of those who believed in him became manifest."

⁕ He said: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Simak, from Ibrahim, concerning His words, ﴿So We supported those who believed against their enemy, and they became dominant﴾: "They were supported by Muhammad ﷺ, who confirmed them and informed of their proof."

⁕ Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, he said: Hushaym narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim, concerning His words, ﴿so they became dominant﴾: "The proof of those who believed in Jesus became manifest by the confirmation of Muhammad ﷺ, the Word of Allah and His Spirit."

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, he said: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His words, ﴿so they became dominant﴾: "Those who believed with Jesus ﷺ."

End of the commentary on Surat al-Saff.
